90048033.s: The Maqsad Quba project is a culturally significant development designed as one of the prominent architectural landmarks that add beauty to Madinah and offer a unique tourist experience, providing integrated services for Madinah's visitors with open plazas and main alley-style walkways overlooking Quba Mosque.
90048033.b:
What is the Maqsad Quba project?

A project of cultural value designed to be one of the prominent architectural landmarks that add beauty to Madinah and offer a unique tourist experience, achieving its core aim of benefiting its target groups by providing integrated services for visitors to Madinah. It contains plazas, open areas and main alley-style walkways overlooking Quba Mosque. The available spaces allow sustainable events in the outdoor plazas, so the project forms an integrated urban fabric that is the destination for everyone coming to Madinah and for its residents, within a system of unique designs that keep pace with the latest engineering innovations, combining the past and present of Madinah and Quba Mosque in particular.

Project Contents

The project is divided into two sections:

Section One:

Commercial showrooms that symbolize Madinah

The experience of this city

A dedicated nursery area serving visitors to Quba Mosque

The Madinah restaurant

Mobile kiosks offering the bounty of Madinah

An information center

Section Two:

Commercial showrooms

A padel court with a Madinah-inspired design

A bird sanctuary

Visitor parking and buses for Umrah pilgrims

Seating areas serving quality of life

Changing seasonal kiosks

90027338.s: The history of the people of Diriyah, spanning 1,400 years up to the Al Saud family.
90027338.b:
The history of the people of Diriyah, spanning 1,400 years up to the Al Saud family.

What can you expect?

Diriyah Gallery takes you on a journey through time spanning more than 1,400 years, telling the story of the people of Diriyah from their first settlement in Wadi Hanifah to the rise of the First Saudi State under the Al Saud family. The gallery relies on modern, interactive display methods that combine archaeological artifacts with visual media, to present an integrated narrative of the social, economic and political life that shaped Diriyah's identity through the ages.

The gallery is in the heart of the historic At-Turaif district, a UNESCO World Heritage site, giving visitors the chance to connect what they see with the surrounding mud-brick buildings and alleys, leaving with a deeper understanding of the depth of Diriyah's historical roots and its pivotal role in the founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

90023210.s: The historic At-Turaif district, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2010, is an architectural masterpiece that embodies the scholarly and cultural development that distinguished the First Saudi State.
90023210.b:
The historic At-Turaif district: the royal district of the First Saudi State.

The historic At-Turaif district, a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2010, is an architectural masterpiece that embodies the scholarly and cultural development that distinguished the First Saudi State.

The buildings of this ancient district are notable for their unique designs, consisting of several floors built using mud and natural materials drawn from the surrounding environment. These buildings have proven their sturdiness and ability to endure for many centuries, standing as a living witness to the genius of architectural creativity of that era.

At-Turaif played a pivotal role as a vibrant center of civilization in Diriyah, capital of the First Saudi State (1727-1818).

89707768.s: From the earth to the moon, and from prehistoric times to the modern era, the halls of the Saudi National Museum take you on a fascinating journey beyond time and place, in the heart of Riyadh in the Al Murabba district, next to King Abdulaziz Palace.
89707768.b:
About the Saudi National Museum

From the earth to the moon, and from prehistoric times to the modern era, the halls of the Saudi National Museum take you on a fascinating journey beyond time and place, standing before artistic and historical evidence in the heart of Riyadh in the Al Murabba district, next to King Abdulaziz Palace. The museum opened in 1419 AH on an area of 17,000 square meters, where the stories of 3,700 heritage pieces unfold, including statues, manuscripts and sculptures like no others.

The Saudi National Museum has eight sections filled with the spirit of history, beginning in the Man and the Universe Hall, where you learn about the origin of the universe and the solar system, and the natural factors that have influenced its development over millions of years. The Ancient Arabian Kingdoms Hall lets you immerse yourself in civilizations that spanned from the fourth millennium BC to the second century AD, while patterns of religious and social life before Islam appear in the Pre-Islamic Era Hall. The life of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is shown in the Prophetic Mission Hall, from the revelation until his migration to Madinah. The history of the unification of the Kingdom appears in a documentary film in the Unification of the Kingdom Hall, and the Hajj and the Two Holy Mosques Hall covers aspects of the architectural development of the Grand Mosque and the Prophet's Mosque.

89707529.s: One kilometer southwest of Qasr Al Hukm, Addoho Neighborhood lies in the heart of Riyadh and is the last of the old districts to preserve its traditional Najdi urban fabric. 89707529.b: One kilometer southwest of Qasr Al Hukm, Addoho Neighborhood lies in the heart of Riyadh and is the last of the old districts to preserve its traditional Najdi urban fabric. Addoho was built more than 200 years ago. From its strategic location within the Qasr Al Hukm area and its historical landmarks, to its narrow alleys and the details of its houses that express the way of life of local residents at the time, Addoho tells the story of a desert civilization whose buildings were surrounded by walls and palm trees.
